samples.question: This picture shows two square panels drawn far apart, one near the left edge and one near the right edge. Each panel is a five-row, five-column grid of cells, and every cell carries exactly one of two flat tones, dark or pale; both tones appear inside both panels. Exactly one of the two panels has a thick solid upright bar drawn against its inner edge, the edge that faces the other panel: that bar is the hinge, and the panel it touches is the hinged panel. A few small clutter squares of a different colour lie on the background between the panels; they are not cells and carry no evidence. Carry out this operation. Fold the hinged panel across its hinge and lay it flat on top of the other panel, so that the hinged panel's grid is mirrored left to right - its column order is reversed, its row order is unchanged - and its cell that lands on a given cell of the other panel is the one in the same row and the mirrored column. Now mark every one of the twenty-five stacked positions where exactly one of the two layers is dark, and leave unmarked every position where both layers are dark and every position where neither is. Exactly nine positions get marked in every picture. The marked positions always form exactly one of five symbols on the five-by-five grid. 'plus' is an upright bar through the middle column crossing a flat bar through the middle row. 'ex' is the two full diagonals crossing at the centre cell. 'tee' is the full top row plus the middle column below it. 'ell' is the full left column plus the full bottom row. 'seven' is the full top row plus a diagonal running from the top-right area down to the bottom-left cell. The symbol is drawn nowhere in the picture and neither panel contains it: each panel on its own is consistent with every symbol, so both distant panels and the hinge must be read together. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, ex, tee, ell, seven.
